post.summary: Posts a journal typed by hand, once
post.description:
Posts a journal typed by hand, once. THE FORM TO CALL: a retry with the same `p_idempotency_key` returns the first call's journal instead of posting a second, and the same key with different arguments is refused rather than quietly answered. A manual journal has no document behind it, so there is no "already posted" flag to catch a repeat -- which is why this overload exists (`0307`). The key has no default, because a call that omits it resolves to the unprotected original. Refuses lines that do not balance and a date outside an open fiscal period. Needs `can_post`.

`public.post_manual_journal(p_org_id uuid, p_entry_date date, p_lines jsonb, p_description text, p_reference text, p_idempotency_key text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

This function is overloaded. Described above is the longest form; also defined: `(p_org_id uuid, p_entry_date date, p_lines jsonb, p_description text, p_reference text, p_idempotency_key text)`. PostgREST picks between them on the argument names in the request body, so omitting one merely-optional argument can resolve to a different function than the one intended — for the idempotency-protected writes, to the unprotected original.

Holds an advisory lock on the site, so two people pressing the button together cannot both pass the check. Refuses when no tenancy covers the period, and that is the only guard against an accidental press on the right dates. `rent_preview` shows what would be raised. The due date defaults to the start of the period. NOTE there is no way to undo a run: the invoices can be voided one at a time, the run row stays. REFUSES A PERIOD ALREADY COVERED by an earlier run, overlapping or identical, naming it. Holds an advisory lock on the scheme. Refuses outright when no rate is in force on the period start — an AGM resolution sets the rate before charges can be raised — and refuses when any parcel has no owner on record, rather than skipping it, because a parcel silently left out of a charge run is one nobody discovers until the fund is short. `strata_charge_preview` shows what would be raised. NOTE there is no way to undo a run. Needs `can_post` and the `property_strata` module.

Books the stock in at the far end and clears goods in transit. `p_counts` is what actually arrived, line by line; a line not named is taken as arriving in full. Refuses a transfer that is not `sent`, and refuses a count larger than what was sent, because there is no such thing as receiving more than left. WHAT IS SHORT IS NOT LOST QUIETLY: the difference is charged to `5900`, the account 0087 already uses for a stock difference nobody can explain, so transit always clears to nil and the loss is on the profit and loss where somebody will see it. Stock arrives at the cost it LEFT at, not the destination's average, because averaging it in would move value between two warehouses of one company. Needs the inventory module.

post.summary: Spends points against a parked bill and returns what was applied
post.description:
Spends points against a parked bill and returns what was applied. Points cannot buy more than the basket: rather than refuse, it takes only what is needed and LEAVES THE REST ON THE ACCOUNT, rounding the points DOWN so that over-redeeming never takes one more point than the basket is worth. Zero clears a redemption thought better of, without voiding the sale. The basket is read from the lines rather than from `total_amount`, which already has any earlier redemption off it — reading that would let two calls stack until the sale was free. Refuses a bill that is not parked, a sale not on a member's account, and anything under the programme's minimum. Needs `can_write_module('loyalty')`.

post.summary: Re-runs every active promotion against a bill and returns the new total
post.description:
Re-runs every active promotion against a bill and returns the new total. Promotions are recomputed rather than remembered, so this is what makes a basket that has just crossed a threshold — spend 50, get 5 off — pick the offer up without the line being re-rung. Safe to call repeatedly; it replaces what it found. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.refresh_pos_sale_promotions(p_sale uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Records a device to send push notifications to, and returns its row
post.description:
Records a device to send push notifications to, and returns its row. Keyed ON THE TOKEN, not on the pair of user and token: one handset is one row, belonging to whoever is signed in on it now, so a colleague signing in on a shared tablet takes the row over rather than adding a second and getting the first person's notifications (0141). A browser subscription must bring its `p256dh` and `auth` keys or there is nothing to encrypt the notification to, and a phone must not bring them; on a re-subscribe the keys are REPLACED rather than merged, because a browser that re-subscribes has thrown the old keypair away. Platform is android, ios or web.

`public.register_device(p_token text, p_platform text, p_label text, p_p256dh text, p_auth text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Undoes a departure
post.description:
Undoes a departure. A resignation withdrawn and a departure recorded against the wrong person are both ordinary, and a state with no way out of it is how somebody deletes an employee record to fix a typo.

`public.reinstate_employee(p_employee uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Records that a withholding certificate has been paid over to the Inland Revenue Board, and posts the payment
post.description:
Records that a withholding certificate has been paid over to the Inland Revenue Board, and posts the payment. The certificate must be POSTED FIRST -- there is nothing to remit until the liability is in the books -- and one already remitted is refused, naming the date. A bank account belonging to another company is REFUSED BY NAME rather than quietly ignored: falling back to the default cash account would post the entry anyway and leave nobody any the wiser. Needs `can_post`.

`public.remit_withholding(p_id uuid, p_paid_on date, p_bank_account_id uuid, p_reference text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Takes a choice back off a line and re-prices the line
post.description:
Takes a choice back off a line and re-prices the line. Refuses once the bill is no longer parked. Silent on a row that is already gone, because a cashier tapping the same X twice has not made a mistake worth a dialog. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.remove_line_modifier(p_line_modifier uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Takes an unsent line off a parked bill
post.description:
Takes an unsent line off a parked bill. Refuses once the kitchen has been told -- that is void_pos_sale_line, which wants a reason.

`public.remove_pos_sale_line(p_line uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Takes one promotion off a parked bill and returns the bill it was on
post.description:
Takes one promotion off a parked bill and returns the bill it was on. No line was ever rewritten to apply it, so there is no price to put back and nothing else changes. Refuses once the bill is settled or voided. Note that `refresh_pos_sale_promotions` will re-apply the same offer if it still qualifies — to hold a bill without it, remove the reason rather than the row. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.remove_pos_sale_promotion(p_row uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Files the replacement for a permit, visa or certificate and returns it, carrying the type, title and notes…
post.description:
Files the replacement for a permit, visa or certificate and returns it, carrying the type, title and notes across unless new ones are given, and linking it to what it supersedes. Refuses to renew a document THAT HAS ALREADY BEEN RENEWED — renew the one that replaced it, not the one it replaced — which is what stops a chain forking into two current permits. Refuses a renewal expiring on or before the document it replaces: that is a different document, and treating it as a renewal would retire the permit that is still the current one. The issue date defaults to the old expiry, so a chain has no gap in it. Needs `can_manage_hr`.

`public.renew_employee_document(p_document uuid, p_expires_date date, p_issued_date date, p_title text, p_notes text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Rent preview
post.description: `public.rent_preview(p_site_id uuid, p_period_from date, p_period_to date)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Reopens one half of an appraisal -- `self`, `manager` or `final` -- by clearing that half's submission stamp…
post.description:
Reopens one half of an appraisal -- `self`, `manager` or `final` -- by clearing that half's submission stamp, which is what the guard reads when it refuses a change. NOTHING WRITTEN IS ERASED: the author comes back to their own words and edits them rather than starting from a blank box. Any other side name is refused. Needs `can_manage_hr`.

`public.reopen_appraisal(p_appraisal uuid, p_side text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Reopens a completed bank reconciliation
post.description:
Reopens a completed bank reconciliation. Refuses if the SAME ACCOUNT has been reconciled again to a later statement date, naming that date and saying to reopen it first -- reopening an earlier one would release lines the later one was closed over, and that later reconciliation balanced against having them. Nothing about the matching itself is undone: the lines go back to matched-but-unclosed, which is what they were a moment before it was completed. Needs `can_post`.

`public.reopen_bank_reconciliation(p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Puts a lost lead back in play
post.description:
Puts a lost lead back in play. Returns it to CONTACTED rather than to new, because somebody did speak to them and pretending otherwise loses the only thing the record knew. Refuses a lead that is not lost. Needs `can_write`.

`public.reopen_lead(p_lead uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Reopens a closed file
post.description:
Reopens a closed file. A client coming back and a matter closed by somebody who picked the wrong row are both ordinary, and the alternative is a second matter for the same job with the client's money split across two files.

`public.reopen_matter(p_matter uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Puts a closed deal back in play, at the stage given or the one it was working in
post.description:
Puts a closed deal back in play, at the stage given or the one it was working in. Never at the stage it DIED in: that is a closed column, and a deal sitting in it would read as closed again. Falls back to the first open stage when neither is available, and refuses if the pipeline has no open stage at all. Refuses a deal already open. Needs `can_write`.

`public.reopen_opportunity(p_opportunity uuid, p_stage uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Makes a closed project active again so time and cost can be booked to it
post.description:
Makes a closed project active again so time and cost can be booked to it. Refuses one already open. Needs `can_post` rather than `can_write` -- a reopened project is somewhere the ledger can be told to put money.

`public.reopen_project(p_project uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Lets the customer answer their own ticket through the share link, without an account
post.description:
Lets the customer answer their own ticket through the share link, without an account. WRITES: a comment, always visible -- `is_internal` defaults to TRUE and a customer's own message landing as an internal note would be invisible to the person who sent it -- plus a `requester_reply` event, and the ticket reopens if it was pending, on hold, resolved or closed. `first_response_at` is deliberately left alone: the first-response target is a promise the company made about how quickly IT would answer, and stopping that clock on the customer's own message would report a target met that nobody met. An empty body is refused.

`public.reply_to_shared_ticket(p_token text, p_body text)` Writes. Reachable without signing in.

post.summary: Lets the app write down a refusal the database never saw — one the client enforced itself, which would…
post.description:
Lets the app write down a refusal the database never saw — one the client enforced itself, which would otherwise leave no trace of somebody probing at doors. RETURNS QUIETLY rather than raising when the caller is not in the company: taking the caller's word for the organization would let anybody write into anybody's log, and a refusal aimed at a company you are not in is not that company's event. RATE LIMITED to one a minute per person, so a loop cannot bury the rest of the log — which means a burst of refusals appears as one entry, and the count is not the number of attempts.

`public.report_denied(p_org_id uuid, p_action text, p_message text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.description:
Lets the browser tell the audit log that a password was rejected, which Supabase's own sign-in does not tell this database. Returns void in every branch INCLUDING the branch where the address is unknown: a function that behaved differently for an address that exists would be a way to find out which addresses exist. WRITES: at most one `sign_in`/`refused` security event per account per minute, so a stranger cannot push the events that matter off the end of an auditor's screen.

`public.report_failed_sign_in(p_email text)` Writes. Reachable without signing in.

post.summary: Files a bug report or a suggestion, and is the ONE WRITE IN THIS API THAT DOES NOT STAY WITH THE TENANT…

Files a bug report or a suggestion, and is the ONE WRITE IN THIS API THAT DOES NOT STAY WITH THE TENANT: `feedback_reports` is the platform's table, read by whoever runs the service rather than by the company. `p_org_id` is optional and is only a label saying which company the person was in at the time -- it is checked for membership when given, so it cannot be used to file against somebody else. `p_severity` is kept only for a bug; a severity on a suggestion is dropped rather than refused. Needs a signed-in user and a one-line title, and nothing else.

`public.report_feedback(p_title text, p_kind app.feedback_kind, p_body text, p_screen text, p_app_version text, p_severity smallint, p_org_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.description:
The customer who asks after paying. Re-bills a completed counter sale to an identified buyer and raises their own e-Invoice — and refuses once the sale has been consolidated, because that submission has already told LHDN the buyer was anonymous.

`public.request_einvoice_for_sale(p_sale uuid, p_contact uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.description:
Asks the platform for an address on our mail domain, personal to somebody when `p_owner_id` is given. That person must be an active member of the company — an address for somebody who does not work here would be an address its owner could not read. Needs `can_admin` and the `mailbox` module. Unlike `request_subdomain` this does NOT replace a standing request: a company has many addresses, so each ask is its own row, and a local part already taken is refused.

`public.request_mailbox(p_org_id uuid, p_local_part text, p_owner_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Asks a company admin for temporary sight of payslips, and returns the request
post.description:
Asks a company admin for temporary sight of payslips, and returns the request. ONLY AN AUDITOR MAY ASK: somebody who can already run payroll is told they have access rather than given a second route to it, and anybody else is refused. A reason is required — an unexplained request for other people's pay is the one nobody should be able to file. One live request at a time, which keeps the admin's queue honest.

`public.request_payslip_access(p_org_id uuid, p_reason text, p_period_from date, p_period_to date, p_run_id uuid, p_employee_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Asks the platform for a name on our domain
post.description:
Asks the platform for a name on our domain. ASKING AGAIN REPLACES THE STANDING REQUEST, which is what somebody who has been refused will do — the previous decision and note are cleared with it. An address already APPROVED is not quietly swapped: it is a live door, and changing it is an operator's decision rather than a form submission, so this refuses and says to ask. Needs `can_admin` and the `workspace_address` module. The name is normalised and checked before it is stored; a name already taken is refused rather than queued behind the company that has it.

`public.request_subdomain(p_org_id uuid, p_subdomain text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Puts a dish back on TODAY, undoing an 86
post.description:
Puts a dish back on TODAY, undoing an 86. Returns whether there was anything to undo. The stop is dated in Kuala Lumpur time and is only ever for today, so a kitchen that runs out at eight does not have to remember to put it back tomorrow morning. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.resume_pos_item(p_outlet uuid, p_item uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Puts a counting till back into service
post.description:
Puts a counting till back into service. A count is not a commitment, and a state with no way out of it is how somebody closes a shift early to take one sale.

`public.resume_pos_shift(p_shift uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Rebuilds bank_accounts.current_balance from posted ledger lines
post.description:
Rebuilds bank_accounts.current_balance from posted ledger lines. Assumes each bank account maps to its own GL account, which is the normal setup.

`public.resync_bank_balance(p_bank_account_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Removes an account from the chart if it can be removed and switches it off if it cannot, returning 'deleted'…
post.description:
Removes an account from the chart if it can be removed and switches it off if it cannot, returning 'deleted' or 'deactivated' so the caller can say which happened. Anything ever posted to it, a non-zero opening balance, or any other row still naming it -- a bank account, a budget line, an item's posting account -- means deactivated: deleting would take a balance out of the trial balance or answer with a constraint name instead of a sentence. Refuses outright for an account the ledger posts to by number, which can be renamed but not removed, and for one that still has accounts under it. Needs `can_post`.

`public.retire_account(p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Switches a standing forecast line off
post.description:
Switches a standing forecast line off. NOT A DELETE, despite sitting beside three that are: it sets `is_active` false, because a forecast circulated last month was run against these rows and deleting one makes it impossible to explain why the figure was what it was. Raises `P0002` for a row that is not there rather than returning false, which is the opposite of the three deletes in this migration. Needs the accounting module.

`public.retire_cash_forecast_item(p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `accounting` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Switches a counter off
post.description:
Switches a counter off. RETIRED, NEVER DELETED — `pos_kitchen_tickets.station_id` cascades on delete, so removing the row would remove every docket the counter ever received and destroy a day of kitchen history for somebody tidying a list. Refuses while any ticket on it is still new, cooking or ready: retiring the station takes those off every screen at once, and the plate does not stop existing because a list was tidied. Refuses to retire the outlet's default counter while another is active — make something else the default first, or unrouted dishes have nowhere to go. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.retire_kitchen_station(p_station uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Switches a tier off
post.description:
Switches a tier off. Retired rather than deleted: members drop to whichever band is below it, and a shop that retired one by mistake can put it back. Needs `can_write_module('loyalty')`.

`public.retire_loyalty_tier(p_tier uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `loyalty` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Switches a delivery area off
post.description:
Switches a delivery area off. Retired, never deleted: every delivery already taken names the zone it was charged under, and the fee it was charged at has to stay explicable. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.retire_pos_delivery_zone(p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Stands a driver down
post.description:
Stands a driver down. Refused while they still have orders out, because the shop would lose the only name attached to food that is on a motorbike right now.

`public.retire_pos_driver(p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Switches off a public ordering link
post.description:
Switches off a public ordering link. Switched off rather than deleted: the orders that came in through it still name it. A sticker somebody has to go and peel off is a sticker that should STOP WORKING the moment it is switched off, which is what this does. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.retire_pos_menu_link(p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Switches a menu period off — breakfast, happy hour
post.description:
Switches a menu period off — breakfast, happy hour. The dishes on it go back to always-on rather than losing their grouping, which is why this is a switch and not a delete. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.retire_pos_menu_schedule(p_schedule uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Takes one answer off the menu without deleting it, so what was ordered on it stays answerable
post.description:
Takes one answer off the menu without deleting it, so what was ordered on it stays answerable.

`public.retire_pos_modifier(p_modifier uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Stops a question being asked, and says how many dishes that affects
post.description:
Stops a question being asked, and says how many dishes that affects. The attachments are kept so bringing it back brings the menu wiring with it.

`public.retire_pos_modifier_group(p_group uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Switches an offer off
post.description:
Switches an offer off. Bills it already discounted keep the discount — `refresh_pos_sale_promotions` only stops applying it to new ones — so this ends an offer rather than reversing it. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.retire_pos_promotion(p_promo uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Restates foreign-currency balances at the rate ruling on the date, posting the gain or loss
post.description:
Restates foreign-currency balances at the rate ruling on the date, posting the gain or loss. Undoes its own previous standing revaluation first, dated the same day, so running it twice does not compound: the figure is always the difference from cost, never from the last run. Needs `can_post`. Returns the journal's id.

`public.revalue_foreign_balances(p_org_id uuid, p_as_at date)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Deferred revenue not yet released, one row per period end — the shape recognise_revenue posts in
post.description:
Deferred revenue not yet released, one row per period end — the shape recognise_revenue posts in. Groups totalling zero are omitted because the run skips them.

`public.revenue_schedule_due(p_org_id uuid)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Posts the contra of a journal: the same lines with debit and credit swapped, dated today or the date given…
post.description:
Posts the contra of a journal: the same lines with debit and credit swapped, dated today or the date given, numbered as a new journal and marked `is_reversal` pointing back at the original. The original STAYS POSTED, which reads as an omission and is the design -- the pair nets to zero and both halves are on the page where an auditor can see what happened. Refuses a journal that is not posted, one already reversed (reversing twice would contra the contra and put the entry back), a date no fiscal period covers, and a date whose period is not open. Returns the new journal's id.

`public.reverse_gl_entry(p_entry_id uuid, p_date date)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Turns off a customer's standing portal link -- the one that shows them everything outstanding rather than a…
post.description:
Turns off a customer's standing portal link -- the one that shows them everything outstanding rather than a single document. Their invoices, payments and documents are all unaffected: what ends is their ability to look at them without being chased. Needs `can_write`.

`public.revoke_customer_portal(p_contact_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Turns off every share link for one sales document at once, and returns how many it turned off
post.description:
Turns off every share link for one sales document at once, and returns how many it turned off. A link already sent stops working immediately: `open_shared_document` answers with the state `revoked` and no document. The record of who opened it and when is kept -- revoking removes the access, not the evidence of it. Needs `can_write`.

`public.revoke_document_share(p_document_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Withdraws an employee's approved access to their own payslips, with a note saying why
post.description:
Withdraws an employee's approved access to their own payslips, with a note saying why. Only an APPROVED request can be revoked -- a pending one is declined, not revoked, and the two read differently to the person waiting. Needs `can_admin`, not merely `can_write`: payslip access is the company's own people's pay.

`public.revoke_payslip_access(p_request_id uuid, p_note text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Turns off every share link for one support ticket, returning the count
post.description:
Turns off every share link for one support ticket, returning the count. The customer's link stops opening and stops accepting replies. The conversation itself is untouched; what goes is the way in. Needs the `ticketing` module.

`public.revoke_ticket_share(p_ticket uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `ticketing` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: The same rule one level up: which counter makes everything in this category, in this outlet
post.description:
The same rule one level up: which counter makes everything in this category, in this outlet. An item with its own routing wins over this; a null station clears it and lets the category fall back to the outlet default. Refuses a counter that is not in the named outlet. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.route_category_to_station(p_category uuid, p_outlet uuid, p_station uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Says which counter makes this dish IN THIS OUTLET — the same item in another shop keeps its own routing…
post.description:
Says which counter makes this dish IN THIS OUTLET — the same item in another shop keeps its own routing, which is why the table is not unique on item alone. A null station clears the rule and lets the item fall back to its category's. Refuses a counter that is not in the named outlet. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.route_item_to_station(p_item uuid, p_outlet uuid, p_station uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Charges depreciation on every active asset up to a date, posts one journal grouped by expense and accumulated…
post.description:
Charges depreciation on every active asset up to a date, posts one journal grouped by expense and accumulated account, and returns the run. SAFE TO RUN TWICE: it computes what each asset SHOULD stand at on the date and charges only the difference, so a second run on the same date charges nothing, deletes its own empty run and returns NULL. A null return is therefore "there was nothing to do", not a failure. Assets acquired after the date are skipped and one that reaches cost less residual is marked fully depreciated. Refuses when the chart has no 6400 or 1590 and the asset names no accounts of its own — a journal that cannot name both sides is not one to guess at. Needs `can_post`.

`public.run_depreciation(p_org_id uuid, p_as_at date)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Forecasts every stocked item and records what it decided
post.description:
Forecasts every stocked item and records what it decided. Items with too little history get a line saying so rather than no line at all — an item silently absent from a replenishment report is one nobody notices they stopped ordering.

`public.run_inventory_forecast(p_org uuid, p_warehouse uuid, p_as_of date)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `forecasting` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Cuts one item up into others — a carcass into cuts, a drum into bottles — moving stock out of the source and…
post.description:
Cuts one item up into others — a carcass into cuts, a drum into bottles — moving stock out of the source and into the outputs, with the source's cost split across them by `cost_share`. NOT IDEMPOTENT, and not meant to be: each call is a real conversion that really happened, so calling it twice converts twice. Refuses when there is not enough in the store, unless the company allows negative stock, and refuses when a batch-tracked source has less in traceable lots than the run would consume — the quantity and the lots can disagree, and the lots are what a recall follows. Needs `can_write_module('inventory')`.

`public.run_item_conversion(p_conversion uuid, p_times numeric, p_warehouse uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Runs a saved report and returns one row per group: the dimension values as text, the measures as numbers…
post.description:
Runs a saved report and returns one row per group: the dimension values as text, the measures as numbers, both in the order the report declared.

`public.run_pos_report(p_report uuid, p_from date, p_to date)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Raises every recurring document due on or before a date for ONE company, and returns how many
post.description:
Raises every recurring document due on or before a date for ONE company, and returns how many. Safe to run twice on the same day: raising a document advances its `next_run_date`, so the second call finds nothing due. A date in the past will raise every occurrence that was missed, which is the intended way to catch up and is not what you want if you were only re-running today. Needs `can_post`.

`public.run_recurring_documents_for(p_org_id uuid, p_on date)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: The same for recurring journals, one company, returning how many were advanced
post.description:
The same for recurring journals, one company, returning how many were advanced. Two things a caller will not expect. First, a template with `auto_post` OFF POSTS NOTHING but still has its schedule advanced — it is counted in the return and no entry exists. Second, a template that throws does not stop the others: the error is written to `last_error` on that row and the loop carries on, so a return of 9 out of 10 is silent, and `last_error_at` is the only place it shows. Deliberately not `app.run_recurring_journals`, which walks every organization in the database; a signed-in user may only post in their own. Needs `can_post`.

`public.run_recurring_journals_for(p_org_id uuid, p_on date)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Scale formats list
post.description: `public.scale_formats_list(p_org uuid)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Mail matching a search, both directions, newest first
post.description:
Mail matching a search, both directions, newest first. Invoker rights: 0559's policies decide whose mail is searched. 0561.

`public.search_mail(p_org_id uuid, p_query text, p_mailbox_id uuid, p_limit integer)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Seats a table from a register and returns the bill to work on, opening one only if the table has none
post.description:
Seats a table from a register and returns the bill to work on, opening one only if the table has none. Tapping an occupied table therefore RESUMES that bill rather than starting a second, which is what a waiter walking back to a table means. Covers can be corrected on the way past: a two-top that became a four-top is the normal case, not an error. Refuses a table out of service, a table in another outlet — a waiter cannot seat a table they are not standing in — and a table with more than one bill open, where it asks which. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.seat_table(p_register uuid, p_table uuid, p_covers integer)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Returns who signed in, from what address, who exported, who read something sensitive and who was refused
post.description:
Returns who signed in, from what address, who exported, who read something sensitive and who was refused. A READ THAT WRITES, and this is the one where that matters most: the body says a security log that does not record who read it is the one record an insider has no reason to avoid. Do not poll it. Capped at 1,000 rows. Owner or administrator only — it says where every colleague works from, which is the same bar as the audit trail and for a sharper reason.

`public.security_log(p_org_id uuid, p_kind app.security_event, p_since timestamp with time zone, p_limit integer)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Security summary
post.description: `public.security_summary(p_org_id uuid, p_days integer)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Queues a message from one of the company's addresses, optionally as a reply and optionally with one file
post.description:
Queues a message from one of the company's addresses, optionally as a reply and optionally with one file. Queued, never sent: send-email drains the outbox. 0560, attachment 0565.

`public.send_from_mailbox(p_mailbox_id uuid, p_to text, p_subject text, p_body text, p_in_reply_to uuid, p_attachment_path text, p_attachment_name text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Prints the dockets: takes every line the kitchen has NOT yet seen, routes each to its station, and returns…
post.description:
Prints the dockets: takes every line the kitchen has NOT yet seen, routes each to its station, and returns one row per docket made. Sending twice sends only what was added since — the second round does not re-cook the first, and a station that already had a ticket from an earlier round gets a new one rather than having a line appended to something that may already be cooking. A PAID bill can still be sent: a kiosk and a fast-food counter take the money and then cook. Only a voided one refuses, along with a bill that still has unanswered "choose one" questions — a cook cannot guess — or a dish nothing routes and no default station to catch it. Needs `can_write_module('pos')`.

`public.send_order_to_kitchen(p_sale uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Takes stock out of the sending store and puts its value in goods in transit -- debit transit, credit…
post.description:
Takes stock out of the sending store and puts its value in goods in transit -- debit transit, credit inventory -- so the stock is on neither shelf and the balance sheet still has it. Refuses a transfer that is not `draft`, and one with no lines. Refuses more than the store holds unless the company has allowed negative stock, and refuses more than its BATCHES hold whatever that setting says, because a van cannot carry a batch nobody has. Needs the inventory module.

`public.send_stock_transfer(p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Stores a company's own key for one AI provider, so the assistant bills them rather than us
post.description:
Stores a company's own key for one AI provider, so the assistant bills them rather than us. Refuses an unknown provider, an empty key, and a provider that needs a base URL given without one. Needs `can_admin`.

`public.set_ai_credentials(p_org_id uuid, p_provider text, p_api_key text, p_base_url text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: One company's choice of provider, model and whose key pays
post.description:
One company's choice of provider, model and whose key pays. The model must be one the platform lists when the platform's key pays for it, and may be any the provider answers to when the company brings its own.

`public.set_ai_settings(p_org_id uuid, p_enabled boolean, p_provider text, p_model text, p_key_source text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Pauses or resumes the automatic statement feed on one bank account
post.description:
Pauses or resumes the automatic statement feed on one bank account. Pausing stops new statement lines arriving; it does not disconnect the feed or discard what has already come in. Needs `can_admin`.

`public.set_bank_feed_paused(p_bank_account_id uuid, p_paused boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Moves a table booking along
post.description:
Moves a table booking along. `arrived` and `completed` CANNOT be set here: they are claims about money and stock, and checking in and settling the sale are the only things entitled to make them. A completed booking cannot be moved at all. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.set_booking_status(p_booking uuid, p_status app.pos_booking_status, p_note text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Replaces a budget's lines wholesale and returns how many were written
post.description:
Replaces a budget's lines wholesale and returns how many were written. DRAFT ONLY: an approved budget is what variance is reported against, and rewriting it underneath a report already circulated would change what people were told without changing the report. A ZERO IS NOT A LINE and is dropped rather than stored -- keeping them would fill the grid with rows that say nothing and make "which accounts are budgeted" unanswerable. Refuses an account that does not exist or is a heading, and a period outside the budget's year.

`public.set_budget_lines(p_budget uuid, p_lines jsonb)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `accounting` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Writes what SSM's register answered onto a contact, and stamps `ssm_verified_at`
post.description:
Writes what SSM's register answered onto a contact, and stamps `ssm_verified_at`. OVERWRITES THE NAME AND THE REGISTRATION NUMBER: that is the point — the registry is the authority on both, and a lookup somebody confirmed is worth more than what was typed off a letterhead. Does NOT overwrite `id_value` when the contact already has one, because a TIN entered deliberately for e-Invoice is not this function's to replace; it only fills an empty one, as BRN. The old registration number is kept when the registry does not return one, since an older number that was already recorded is still true. Needs `can_write`.

`public.set_contact_ssm_entity(p_contact uuid, p_name text, p_reg_no text, p_reg_no_old text, p_entity_type text, p_slug text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Switches one custom field on or off for an entity type
post.description:
Switches one custom field on or off for an entity type. Switching off hides the field from forms and keeps every value already recorded against it, so turning it back on restores the data rather than an empty column. Refuses a field that does not exist on that entity, naming both. Needs `can_admin`.

`public.set_custom_field_active(p_org_id uuid, p_entity text, p_key text, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Set a series -- prefix, suffix, padding, reset policy, next number -- and return the sample of the next number
post.description:
Set a series -- prefix, suffix, padding, reset policy, next number -- and return the sample of the next number. Admin only. The next number cannot go below the last issued while the series keeps its prefix, suffix and reset policy. See 0480.

`public.set_document_numbering(p_org_id uuid, p_doc_type text, p_prefix text, p_suffix text, p_padding integer, p_reset_policy text, p_next_value bigint)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Stores a company's MyInvois credentials and signing certificate for one environment, sandbox or production…
post.description:
Stores a company's MyInvois credentials and signing certificate for one environment, sandbox or production, replacing what was there. The environment must be one of those two by name. The client secret may be omitted on a later call to keep the one already stored -- so a screen can show the certificate details and save them without having the secret to re-send -- but it must be present the FIRST time, and the function says so rather than storing a row that cannot authenticate. Needs `can_admin`.

`public.set_einvoice_credentials(p_org_id uuid, p_environment text, p_client_id text, p_client_secret text, p_cert_pem text, p_cert_private_key_pem text, p_cert_serial_number text, p_cert_issuer_name text, p_cert_expires_at timestamp with time zone)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Replace an expense's split
post.description:
Replace an expense's split. The header amount, tax and account are written from the lines. See 0496.

`public.set_expense_split(p_expense_id uuid, p_lines jsonb)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Moves a piece of feedback somebody sent us along, with a note
post.description:
Moves a piece of feedback somebody sent us along, with a note. Platform administrators only: this is our own queue, not a tenant's.

`public.set_feedback_status(p_id uuid, p_status app.feedback_status, p_note text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Opens, closes or LOCKS a fiscal period, which decides what the ledger will take: posting is refused outside…
post.description:
Opens, closes or LOCKS a fiscal period, which decides what the ledger will take: posting is refused outside an open period, so this is the switch behind every "the period is closed" refusal elsewhere. Three statuses and no others. LOCKED IS TERMINAL -- a locked period cannot be reopened by any path, because that is what year-end sign-off means, and a lock somebody can undo is not a sign-off. Needs `can_admin`: closing the books is not a bookkeeping act.

`public.set_fiscal_period_status(p_period_id uuid, p_status text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: States what share of THIS company the parent holds, which is what consolidation is computed from
post.description:
States what share of THIS company the parent holds, which is what consolidation is computed from. Needs `can_admin` of the company being owned and deliberately NOT of the parent: this is a fact about this company's share capital, and the person who runs it is the one who knows it. The parent must be in the same group and one the caller can already reach -- the rule `link_group_contact` uses, for the same reason: otherwise this becomes a way to discover which companies exist. Refuses a company owning itself, and a percentage outside nought to a hundred.

`public.set_group_ownership(p_org_id uuid, p_parent_org_id uuid, p_percent numeric)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Sets which questions a dish is sold with, in the order they will be asked
post.description:
Sets which questions a dish is sold with, in the order they will be asked. The array is the whole answer: anything not in it is detached.

`public.set_item_modifier_groups(p_item uuid, p_groups uuid[])` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Puts an item on a stall in a food court, or takes it off with null
post.description:
Puts an item on a stall in a food court, or takes it off with null. The stall must be this company's, refused by name rather than ignored. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.set_item_stall(p_item uuid, p_stall uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Marks an item as sold by weight, with the PLU the scale prints
post.description:
Marks an item as sold by weight, with the PLU the scale prints. Refuses it unless the item's unit actually measures something -- a kilogram, a litre -- because a third of a box is not a quantity and neither is a third of a piece. Needs the `inventory` module.

`public.set_item_weighed(p_item uuid, p_weighed boolean, p_plu text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Records which batches or serial numbers a line is made up of, and returns how many were recorded
post.description:
Records which batches or serial numbers a line is made up of, and returns how many were recorded. Refused for sales lines -- those take their lots at picking, not at entry. Refuses an item not tracked by batch or serial, a line with no reference, and a quantity of nothing. A serial is one unit by definition, so the screen cannot say otherwise. All of it is refused HERE rather than at posting, deliberately: the person who knows which boxes they picked is the one looking at this line now; the one who finds out at posting is whoever presses the button a week later.

`public.set_line_lots(p_line_table text, p_line_id uuid, p_lots jsonb)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Puts a member on an access type -- the named bundle of permissions this company defined -- or takes them off…
post.description:
Puts a member on an access type -- the named bundle of permissions this company defined -- or takes them off it with null. The access type must belong to the SAME company, refused by name rather than ignored: an id from another company's list would otherwise be silently dropped and read as applied. Needs `can_admin`.

`public.set_member_access_type(p_member_id uuid, p_access_type_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Changes a membership's status and returns what it became
post.description:
Changes a membership's status and returns what it became. Ending a membership -- cancelled or expired -- ALSO STOPS ITS RECURRING BILLING, and that second half is the point: a cancelled member who keeps receiving invoices is the complaint that reaches the regulator. Needs the `memberships` module.

`public.set_membership_status(p_subscription uuid, p_status app.pos_membership_status)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `memberships` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Puts a module away, or brings it back, for one company
post.description:
Puts a module away, or brings it back, for one company. The test is ENTITLEMENT, not whether a row happens to exist: `0233`'s backfill left `is_enabled = false` rows on companies that do not hold the module, and a "no row" test let those straight through -- which is what the production probe caught. You cannot put away something you were never given. Needs `can_admin`.

Re-photographs a recurring schedule's template from an existing document, which must be an invoice for a sales schedule or a bill for a purchase one, not deleted, AND BELONGING TO THE SAME COMPANY -- copying across organizations would put one company's prices into another's billing. The snapshot is taken once, here: later edits to that document do not reach the schedule. This is also the repair for a schedule that bills short, because `app.snapshot_document` whitelists the header columns it copies, so a column added to the document table after the snapshot was taken is missing from everything raised off it -- `0416` (service charge) and `0441` (the tax on it) were both that, and re-pointing the schedule at a document raised today picks them up. IT ALSO MOVES THE CUSTOMER: `contact_id` is overwritten from the source document, so copying from an invoice raised for somebody else re-aims every future run at them. Nothing else about the schedule changes -- frequency, next run date and occurrence count are left alone. Needs posting rights.

post.description:
Creates or edits one model under a provider, with its context window and whether it is free. Refuses a provider that does not exist and a model with no id: a model has to be named to be called. Platform administrators only.

`public.upsert_ai_model(p_provider text, p_model_id text, p_name text, p_kind text, p_is_free boolean, p_context_tokens integer, p_notes text, p_is_active boolean, p_sort_order integer)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Creates or edits an AI provider in the platform's catalogue -- how to reach it, whether it needs a key, and…
post.description:
Creates or edits an AI provider in the platform's catalogue -- how to reach it, whether it needs a key, and what a key looks like so an operator can tell they have pasted the right thing. Platform administrators only.

`public.upsert_ai_provider(p_code text, p_name text, p_wire text, p_base_url text, p_docs_url text, p_key_hint text, p_needs_key boolean, p_is_active boolean, p_sort_order integer)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Adds or amends a bank account and the GL account behind it, as one act, so the two cannot disagree
post.description:
Adds or amends a bank account and the GL account behind it, as one act, so the two cannot disagree.

`public.upsert_bank_account(p_name text, p_bank_name text, p_bank_code text, p_account_number text, p_account_type text, p_currency text, p_account_id uuid, p_id uuid, p_org_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Creates or renames a budget for a financial year
post.description:
Creates or renames a budget for a financial year. An APPROVED budget is refused: it is what variance is reported against, and changing it underneath a report already circulated would change what people were told without changing the report. The lines are `set_budget_lines`, separately and under the same rule. Needs the `accounting` module.

`public.upsert_budget(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_year uuid, p_name text, p_department text, p_notes text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `accounting` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits one of the things only a person knows -- a payment expected or promised that no invoice or…
post.description:
Creates or edits one of the things only a person knows -- a payment expected or promised that no invoice or bill has yet recorded -- so the thirteen-week forecast can include it. Refuses a description like "Payment" that tells a later reader nothing, an amount of nothing, and a recurrence that ends before it starts. Needs the `accounting` module.

`public.upsert_cash_forecast_item(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_direction text, p_description text, p_amount numeric, p_expected_on date, p_recurrence text, p_until date, p_notes text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `accounting` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a custom field on a master record
post.description:
Creates or edits a custom field on a master record. THE KEY IS DERIVED FROM THE LABEL THE FIRST TIME AND FROZEN AFTER: renaming the label later changes what people read and not where the values live, so existing data stays attached. Refuses an entity that cannot carry custom fields, a label nobody can read, and a kind outside text, number, date, boolean, select and lookup. Needs `can_admin`.

`public.upsert_custom_field(p_org_id uuid, p_entity text, p_label text, p_key text, p_kind text, p_is_required boolean, p_options jsonb, p_target_entity text, p_help_text text, p_min_value numeric, p_max_value numeric, p_max_length integer, p_show_on_list boolean, p_sort_order integer)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Defines what a bundle is made of
post.description:
Defines what a bundle is made of. Writes the same rows a POS recipe does, because they are the same idea.

`public.upsert_item_bundle(p_org uuid, p_item uuid, p_lines jsonb, p_notes text, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a conversion -- one item broken down into several, a carcass into cuts, a drum into bottles
post.description:
Creates or edits a conversion -- one item broken down into several, a carcass into cuts, a drum into bottles. REPLACES EVERY OUTPUT. Refuses a conversion that starts with nothing, produces nothing, or names an item that is not this company's, and every output needs both an item and a quantity above nought. Needs the `inventory` module.

`public.upsert_item_conversion(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_item uuid, p_qty numeric, p_uom text, p_outputs jsonb, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Says how many base units are in a pack -- a dozen, a case of twenty-four -- so an order in cases becomes a…
post.description:
Says how many base units are in a pack -- a dozen, a case of twenty-four -- so an order in cases becomes a quantity in the books. Refuses a pack of nothing, and refuses the item's OWN base unit: a base unit is one by definition, and a row saying otherwise would silently rescale every quantity the item has. Needs the `inventory` module.

`public.upsert_item_uom_pack(p_item uuid, p_uom text, p_qty numeric)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a kitchen counter that orders are routed to
post.description:
Creates or edits a kitchen counter that orders are routed to. Making one the default clears the previous one IN THE SAME TRANSACTION: the unique partial index rejects a second default outright, and doing it as two calls from the client would leave a moment with no default at all -- which is exactly the moment `send_order_to_kitchen` refuses an unrouted order. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_kitchen_station(p_outlet uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_id uuid, p_sort_order integer, p_is_default boolean, p_is_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a draft landed-cost run -- freight, duty and handling to be spread across the items on one…
post.description:
Creates or edits a draft landed-cost run -- freight, duty and handling to be spread across the items on one or more bills. REPLACES EVERY TARGET AND CHARGE: both lists are deleted and rewritten from what is sent. DRAFT ONLY, because once applied those costs are inside what each item is carried at and every sale since has taken its cost of sales from that figure. A bill must be posted, partly paid or completed to be a target: only a posted bill has moved any stock, and freight can only go onto stock that is there. Needs the `inventory` module.

`public.upsert_landed_cost_run(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_date date, p_bills jsonb, p_charges jsonb, p_notes text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a tier on a loyalty programme -- the points at which it starts and what it multiplies…
post.description:
Creates or edits a tier on a loyalty programme -- the points at which it starts and what it multiplies earning by. Refuses a tier starting below nothing, and refuses a MULTIPLIER OF NOUGHT OR LESS: a tier that earns nothing is a punishment dressed as a reward, and a shop that means "no points" should turn earning off on the scheme itself. Needs the `loyalty` module.

`public.upsert_loyalty_tier(p_program uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_min_points integer, p_multiplier numeric, p_id uuid, p_is_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `loyalty` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Records what MIA's members and firms register said about a corporate officer or a practice, and stamps who…
post.description:
Records what MIA's members and firms register said about a corporate officer or a practice, and stamps who looked it up and when. The owning organization or firm is read FROM THE SUBJECT, never taken from the caller. `verified_via` is always `mia_website_manual`: nothing fetches mia.org.my, and a row that claimed otherwise would be a lie the schema helped tell. Needs `can_write` on the officer's company, or `can_manage_firm` on the firm.

`public.upsert_mia_credential(p_subject_type text, p_subject_id uuid, p_kind app.mia_credential_kind, p_fields jsonb)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Creates or edits a delivery zone for an outlet: the postcodes it covers, the fee, the minimum order, the…
post.description:
Creates or edits a delivery zone for an outlet: the postcodes it covers, the fee, the minimum order, the amount above which delivery is free, and the expected minutes. Postcodes are NORMALISED ON THE WAY IN, so matching an address later is an equality test rather than a function somebody has to remember to call. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_pos_delivery_zone(p_id uuid, p_outlet uuid, p_name text, p_postcodes text[], p_fee numeric, p_min_order numeric, p_free_above numeric, p_eta integer, p_sort integer, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a delivery driver, optionally tied to a user account
post.description:
Creates or edits a delivery driver, optionally tied to a user account. THE USER SHOULD BE SOMEBODY WHO WORKS HERE: pointing the row at a stranger does not fail, and the run is simply assigned and never seen, because row-level security keeps them out of the very rows the app would fetch for them. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_pos_driver(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_name text, p_phone text, p_vehicle text, p_plate text, p_outlet uuid, p_user uuid, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a QR menu link -- the sticker on a table or beside a register
post.description:
Creates or edits a QR menu link -- the sticker on a table or beside a register. A table must belong to the outlet the link is for, refused by name. `p_single` makes it single-use and `p_expires` gives it a life; both are what stop a photographed sticker ordering for ever. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_pos_menu_link(p_outlet uuid, p_kind app.pos_menu_link_kind, p_table uuid, p_register uuid, p_label text, p_expires timestamp with time zone, p_single boolean, p_id uuid, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a menu schedule -- which dishes are orderable on which days and between which hours
post.description:
Creates or edits a menu schedule -- which dishes are orderable on which days and between which hours. Weekdays run 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday), and an hours window needs both ends. The item list is checked BEFORE anything is written, so a bad list does not leave a schedule behind it: `pos_menu_schedule_items_item_same_org` refuses it too since `0522`, but a constraint cannot name the dish. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_pos_menu_schedule(p_org uuid, p_name text, p_weekdays smallint[], p_starts_at time without time zone, p_ends_at time without time zone, p_starts_on date, p_ends_on date, p_items uuid[], p_id uuid, p_is_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits one answer to a modifier group
post.description:
Creates or edits one answer to a modifier group. The price is signed: extra egg is positive, no cucumber is nought, a smaller portion is negative.

`public.upsert_pos_modifier(p_group uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_price_delta numeric, p_id uuid, p_is_default boolean, p_sort_order integer, p_is_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or renames a modifier group -- the question a dish comes with -- including whether the till may…
post.description:
Creates or renames a modifier group -- the question a dish comes with -- including whether the till may answer it with something that is not on the list. Refuses a maximum below the number of answers already ticked by default, because the till starts those selected.

`public.upsert_pos_modifier_group(p_org uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_min_select integer, p_max_select integer, p_id uuid, p_sort_order integer, p_is_active boolean, p_allows_free_text boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Writes a promotion and its scope
post.description:
Writes a promotion and its scope. The scope is written differentially -- only rows that actually joined or left -- so the audit trail 0445 put on those tables reports movement rather than saving.

`public.upsert_pos_promotion(p_org uuid, p_name text, p_kind app.pos_promo_kind, p_code text, p_percent numeric, p_amount numeric, p_buy integer, p_get integer, p_starts_on date, p_ends_on date, p_weekdays smallint[], p_starts_at time without time zone, p_ends_at time without time zone, p_min_subtotal numeric, p_max_uses integer, p_max_per_customer integer, p_items uuid[], p_outlets uuid[], p_channels text[], p_id uuid, p_is_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Saves what an outlet prints — the header and footer on pos_outlets, the choices on pos_receipt_settings — in…
post.description:
Saves what an outlet prints — the header and footer on pos_outlets, the choices on pos_receipt_settings — in one call, so a shop is never left having saved half of it.

`public.upsert_pos_receipt_settings(p_outlet uuid, p_header text, p_footer text, p_paper_mm smallint, p_copies smallint, p_language text, p_item_codes boolean, p_cashier boolean, p_table boolean, p_channel boolean, p_tax boolean, p_customer boolean, p_points boolean, p_qr boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits what a dish is made of, so selling one takes the ingredients off the shelf
post.description:
Creates or edits what a dish is made of, so selling one takes the ingredients off the shelf. REPLACES EVERY LINE. REFUSES A DISH THAT KEEPS ITS OWN STOCK, and that refusal is the design rather than a validation: selling a stock-tracked item already moves it, so a recipe would take the ingredients out a second time. The message names both ways out -- turn tracking off for the dish, or make it with a manufacturing order. Also refuses an item as its own ingredient, and a yield of nothing. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_pos_recipe(p_org uuid, p_item uuid, p_yield numeric, p_lines jsonb, p_notes text, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Saves a built report, checking every key through the same allow-list the query uses — so a report that cannot…
post.description:
Saves a built report, checking every key through the same allow-list the query uses — so a report that cannot run cannot be saved.

`public.upsert_pos_report(p_org uuid, p_name text, p_source app.pos_report_source, p_dimensions text[], p_measures text[], p_period text, p_from date, p_to date, p_outlets uuid[], p_channels text[], p_sort_by text, p_sort_desc boolean, p_limit integer, p_shared boolean, p_id uuid)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a stall in a food court, with the operator who runs it and the commission the court takes
post.description:
Creates or edits a stall in a food court, with the operator who runs it and the commission the court takes. The operator must be a contact of this company. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_pos_stall(p_id uuid, p_outlet uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_operator uuid, p_commission numeric, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Describes how a weighing scale's barcodes are laid out, so the till can read a price or a weight out of the…
post.description:
Describes how a weighing scale's barcodes are laid out, so the till can read a price or a weight out of the label. The prefix must be one to three digits, and prefix plus code digits plus value digits must come to a length a scanner actually produces -- twelve or thirteen with a check digit, eight for the short ones. A format that does not add up would silently mis-read every label it was applied to. Needs the `pos` module.

`public.upsert_scale_format(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_name text, p_prefix text, p_code_digits integer, p_value_digits integer, p_kind app.scale_value_kind, p_check boolean, p_active boolean)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Creates or edits a draft transfer between two of this company's own warehouses
post.description:
Creates or edits a draft transfer between two of this company's own warehouses. REPLACES EVERY LINE: what is sent becomes the whole list, and a line left out is deleted. DRAFT ONLY -- once the transfer is sent, the note is a record of what went on the van, and editing it would change what was recorded as having left. Refuses the same store at both ends, a store that is not this company's, and a transfer with no origin or destination. Needs the `inventory` module.

`public.upsert_stock_transfer(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_from uuid, p_to uuid, p_date date, p_lines jsonb, p_notes text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Records a CDD check as what it is — this document, seen by this individual, on this day
post.description:
Records a CDD check as what it is — this document, seen by this individual, on this day. `id_verified_by` was a column nothing wrote, which left a date asserting that somebody was satisfied without saying who.

`public.verify_person_identity(p_person uuid, p_document_type text, p_verified_on date, p_notes text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Voids a transfer between the company's own bank accounts and reverses its journal if it had one
post.description:
Voids a transfer between the company's own bank accounts and reverses its journal if it had one. Puts back exactly what `post_bank_transfer` took -- the amount SENT, which already includes the fee -- so the two are symmetric and the balance lands where it started. Refuses one already void. The original journal stays posted and a reversing one is added beside it. Needs `can_post`.

`public.void_bank_transfer(p_id uuid, p_reason text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Reverses a contra note, putting the balance back on both the invoices and the bills it settled
post.description:
Reverses a contra note, putting the balance back on both the invoices and the bills it settled. NEEDS WRITE ON BOTH `sales` AND `purchases`, the same pair as creating one -- undoing it touches both ledgers exactly as making it did. Since Sales is core, in practice this turns on Purchases.

`public.void_contra(p_id uuid, p_reason text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Checks more than one module: `purchases`, `sales`. Whether all of them are needed or any one will do is in the description above; it is filed here under the first.

post.summary: Voids a deposit and reverses its journal
post.description:
Voids a deposit and reverses its journal. Refuses one already void, and refuses any deposit that has been touched at all -- applied, refunded or forfeited -- naming the three figures and saying to undo those first, because voiding underneath them would leave allocations pointing at a deposit that never happened.

`public.void_deposit(p_id uuid, p_reason text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Writes off a whole parked bill, behind the pos_void grant without exception: one void record per line the…
post.description:
Writes off a whole parked bill, behind the pos_void grant without exception: one void record per line the kitchen cooked, the live dockets cancelled, and the sale marked voided with a reason and a name. The lines are kept -- they are what was written off.

`public.void_pos_sale(p_sale uuid, p_reason app.pos_void_reason, p_note text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Takes a line off after the kitchen was told, recording what it said, why it went and who did it
post.description:
Takes a line off after the kitchen was told, recording what it said, why it went and who did it. The line is deleted so no downstream arithmetic has to remember to exclude it; the evidence lives in pos_sale_line_voids.

`public.void_pos_sale_line(p_line uuid, p_reason app.pos_void_reason, p_note text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Undoes a rent run: voids every invoice it raised, reversing each one's journal, and frees the period to be…
post.description:
Undoes a rent run: voids every invoice it raised, reversing each one's journal, and frees the period to be raised again. Returns how many invoices were voided. ALL OR NOTHING — it refuses outright when any invoice has a payment against it or has been accepted by LHDN, and says how many, because voiding the rest would free the period while those invoices still stand and the tenants who hold them would be billed a second time. A reason is required: a billing run undone without one is the one the auditor asks about. The run row stays, marked voided, because it is a record of something that happened. Needs `can_post`, the same bar as raising it.

`public.void_rent_run(p_run uuid, p_reason text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Voids an invoice or other sales document and reverses its journal if it had one, recording the reason in…
post.description:
Voids an invoice or other sales document and reverses its journal if it had one, recording the reason in `internal_notes` where the customer will not see it. Refuses outright if any payment has been applied -- a document somebody has paid against is corrected with a credit note, not erased -- and refuses if the e-Invoice is `valid`, because LHDN has it and the cancellation belongs there first. Needs `can_post`.

`public.void_sales_document(p_id uuid, p_reason text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: The same for a strata charge run: voids every invoice, reverses every journal, frees the period, returns the…
post.description:
The same for a strata charge run: voids every invoice, reverses every journal, frees the period, returns the count. Refuses outright when any invoice is paid or accepted by LHDN, for the same reason — a partly undone run whose period is free again bills those owners twice. A reason is required. Needs `can_post`.

`public.void_strata_charge_run(p_run uuid, p_reason text)` Writes. Requires a signed-in user.

post.summary: Weighed items
post.description: `public.weighed_items(p_org uuid)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user. Refused unless the company has the `pos` module and the caller may use it.

post.summary: Resolves a company's own subdomain to the door that should be drawn at it: the name, the logo, the module…
post.description:
Resolves a company's own subdomain to the door that should be drawn at it: the name, the logo, the module, and the login wording if the company wrote any. Only the first label is read, so `sinar.iakauntan.com` and `sinar.staging.iakauntan.com` are one company. Returns nothing unless the reservation is approved AND the company is active or on trial, undeleted, and still has the `workspace_address` module -- an address outliving the company that named it would be a page wearing a stranger's mark. Parked names resolve to nothing, which is the point of parked.

`public.workspace_by_host(p_host text)` Reads only. Reachable without signing in.

post.summary: Null when the signed-in account may open what this address is confined to, otherwise the name of the module…
post.description:
Null when the signed-in account may open what this address is confined to, otherwise the name of the module it lacks.

`public.workspace_module_refusal(p_host text)` Reads only. Requires a signed-in user.

bearerAuth.description: The signed-in user's access token. Every policy and every `app.can_*` guard reads the claims in it, so this is what decides the answer.

apiKey.name: apikey
apiKey.description: The project's anon key. It identifies the project and grants nothing on its own. The service role key is not an alternative to it here: that key bypasses RLS and belongs only in the edge functions.

Refused.description: A guard said no — SQLSTATE 42501. The message is the guard's own words and is meant to be shown.

NotFound.description: No such function, or no such row — SQLSTATE P0002. Under RLS these are the same answer on purpose: whether a row exists is itself something a caller may not be entitled to know.
